accepted.question: In the March 19, 2026 TC AIM RPA chapter, Transport Canada uses “should” and “shall” differently. Which interpretation is correct?
choices: Both words identify mandatory regulatory requirements
“Should” is encouraged practice; “shall” indicates a mandatory procedure supported by regulation
“Should” is mandatory; “shall” is advisory
Neither word has regulatory significance in the TC AIM

accepted.question: A crew member consumed an alcoholic beverage 11 hours and 45 minutes before a planned RPAS flight and is otherwise unimpaired. Under CAR 901.19, may that person act as a crew member?
choices: Yes, because observable impairment is the only restriction
Yes, if the pilot-in-command approves
No, because fewer than 12 hours have elapsed
No, because the required interval is 24 hours

accepted.question: Icing is reported along the intended RPAS route. Under CAR 901.35, which condition can permit the operation with respect to the forecast icing provision?
choices: The aircraft remains below 400 ft AGL
The pilot shortens the flight to less than 15 minutes
The aircraft has de-icing or anti-icing equipment, or the pilot has a means to detect icing
A visual observer watches the propellers continuously

accepted.question: An Advanced RPAS pilot successfully completed an accepted recurrent training activity 23 months ago. Under CAR 901.65, what is the effect on recency for an Advanced operation today?
choices: The pilot remains current because the activity occurred within the preceding 24 months
The pilot is not current because recurrent training is valid for only 12 months
The pilot must complete another flight review before every Advanced flight
Recency never expires once an Advanced certificate has been issued

accepted.question: The TC AIM notes that expanded RPAS regulations effective November 4, 2025 gave Advanced pilots additional privileges. Which is one of those privileges identified by Transport Canada?
choices: Unrestricted BVLOS flight anywhere in Canada
Sheltered operations in any airspace and EVLOS operations in uncontrolled airspace, subject to applicable requirements
Automatic authorization to enter every CYR restricted area
Exemption from the site-survey requirement for EVLOS operations

accepted.question: A VLOS RPA operation is planned 2.5 NM from the centre of an aerodrome operated under the authority of the Minister of National Defence. An established civilian RPAS procedure exists for a nearby airport. What authorization is specifically required by CAR 901.47(4)?
choices: Authorization from the Department of National Defence
Only compliance with the nearby civilian airport procedure
Only an Advanced pilot certificate
No authorization because the operation is more than 1 NM away

held.question: Which item is specifically included among the factors that CAR 901.27 requires a pilot to consider when conducting the site survey?
held.reason: Core CAR 901.27 site-survey factor; likely already represented in flight-planning/site-survey questions.
